title: [finding] docs(protocol): the Backward Compatibility page's pre-1.0 disclaimer still says 0.x, on a platform shipping 17.2.0
body:
Found while linking `content/docs/protocol/backward-compatibility.mdx` back into the site for #12353. Not fixed there: that PR is link repair only, and this is a content-accuracy call.

## The text

`content/docs/protocol/backward-compatibility.mdx`, section `Pre-1.0 Disclaimer`:

> During the **0.x** development phase, MINOR versions may contain breaking changes. The full backward compatibility policy takes effect starting with version **1.0.0**.

The workspace packages are at `17.2.0`.

## Why it is worth a card

The page opens by promising strict backward compatibility guarantees, states a SemVer contract, a three-phase deprecation timeline and a breaking-change table — then ends by telling the reader MINOR may break. Both answers are on one page, and the one that is stale is the one that overrides the rest.

Either the disclaimer is dead text that should be removed (the policy has been in effect since 1.0.0), or something about it is still true and needs restating in v17 terms. That is an editorial call, hence a card rather than a drive-by edit.
